title: 這次廣播的來賓是Daoko，主持人內田敦子提到她是V的認真勢粉絲，每天都會觀看配信，也去了🌸的Sololive。Daoko也承認自己是宅女，還加入了☄️的會員，並提到曾經在廣播節目…
context:
這次廣播的來賓是Daoko，主持人內田敦子提到她是V的認真勢粉絲，每天都會觀看配信，也去了🌸的Sololive。Daoko也承認自己是宅女，還加入了☄️的會員，並提到曾經在廣播節目上與☄️共演過。Daoko也提到自己很喜歡☄️的新專輯，特別是《綺麗事》，得知這首歌是☄️自己作詞作曲後感到驚訝，並給予高度讚賞，讓☄️也對這首歌的評價感到安心。

她談到自己是如何進入V文化的，最初是因為在YouTube上看到🏴‍☠️的MV《美少女無罪》，覺得世界觀很有趣，後來開始看V們的雜談配信，尤其被Holo的氛圍吸引，覺得像是女子高校般親切。

當被問到最推的成員時，Daoko開玩笑表示要在☄️面前說這個可不容易。她說雖然自己是箱推，但最讓她心動的還是🌸。而且她也是☄️的⋯☄️接著說，是我的商業夥伴呢，內田在旁馬上喊  貼貼！

Daoko說她過往從未追過偶像，卻因為🌸第一次產生了「想支持偶像」的心情。她特別欣賞🌸珍惜粉絲的努力，以及她在Live上各種細節的用心，認為作為偶像的🌸是一個值得依靠的存在。☄️也表示她也覺得🌸是一個很適合配信的V。

她最喜歡的🌸的歌曲是《Flower Rhapsody》，這首歌的MV在Sololive後發布，內容讓她和眾多35P感動落淚，覺得自己真的是被自己的推愛著。☄️也認同表示這首MV為演唱會畫下完美句點。

當被問到想對🌸說什麼時，Daoko興奮地表示自己真的很喜歡🌸，並表達會一直支持🌸，只要🌸活著就很感激了。內田說Daoko 真的是粉絲典範。

The guest on this broadcast was Daoko. The host, Uchida Atsuko, mentioned that Daoko is a dedicated fan of Vtubers, watching streams every day and attending 🌸’s sololive. Daoko admitted that she is an otaku, has joined ☄️’s membership, and previously co-starred with ☄️ on a radio show. She also mentioned that she really likes ☄️’s new album, especially Kireigoto, and was surprised to learn that ☄️ wrote and composed the song herself. Her high praise reassured ☄️ about the song’s reception.

Daoko talked about how she got into the Vtuber culture, saying that she first discovered it when she saw 🏴‍☠️’s music video Bishoujo Muzai on YouTube. She found the world-building fascinating and initially thought it was an animated project. Later, she started watching various Vtubers’ talk streams and was especially drawn to Hololive’s atmosphere, which she felt resembled an all-girls high school and made her feel at home.

When asked who her favorite member was, Daoko jokingly said that answering in front of ☄️ made it difficult. She admitted that while she is a full-group supporter, the one who truly captured her heart is 🌸. ☄️ then chimed in, saying, “Ah, my business partner,” to which Uchida immediately reacted with, “TeTe!”

Daoko shared that she had never followed idols before but, for the first time, felt the desire to “support an idol” because of 🌸. She particularly admires 🌸’s dedication to her fans and the care she puts into every detail of her live performances, believing that 🌸 is a truly reliable presence as an idol. ☄️ agreed, saying she also thinks 🌸 is a perfect fit for streaming.

Her favorite song by 🌸 is Flower Rhapsody. The music video was released after 🌸’s sololive, and seeing the live performance scenes in the MV made her and many 35P cry. She felt deeply loved as a fan. ☄️ agreed, saying that the MV provided the perfect closure to the concert experience.

When asked what she would like to say to 🌸, Daoko excitedly expressed that she really loves 🌸 and promised to always support her. She added that just knowing 🌸 is alive makes her feel grateful. Uchida then remarked that Daoko is truly a model fan.

title: Billboard JAPAN ＜訪談＞目標新時代—— Hololive 所屬 虛擬偶像星街彗星高歌「革命」之音樂 Part 1 採訪：Takuto Ueda Hololive 所…
context:
Billboard JAPAN

＜訪談＞目標新時代——
Hololive 所屬
虛擬偶像星街彗星高歌「革命」之音樂

Part 1

採訪：Takuto Ueda

Hololive 所屬的 VTuber／虛擬偶像  星街彗星  推出了全新專輯《新星目錄》。

這是繼前作《Specter》後，睽違約兩年的第三張專輯，並以「革命」作為關鍵詞，是一張充滿挑戰性的作品。收錄了包含氣勢如虹的 VOCALOID 製作人ツミキ所提供的歌曲《ビビデバ》，該曲也成為星街彗星首支累計串流播放量突破 1 億次的歌曲。此外，專輯還集結了山内總一郎（フジファブリック）、川谷繪音（indigo la End、極品下流少女等）、Deu（PEOPLE 1）、なとり、春野等多位風格多元且實力強勁的創作者，共同創作了 11 首樂曲。而專輯的壓軸曲《綺麗事》中，星街彗星也首次挑戰了作詞與作曲。

從出道以來，星街彗星不斷創造「VTuber 史上首次」的成就。「希望 VTuber 更加融入社會」這是她多年來的心願。懷抱著追求新時代的堅定意志，她攜手第三張專輯，並將於 2 月 1 日登上夢想的舞台——日本武道館，舉行個人演唱會。在這個重大的轉折點來臨之際，她回顧了專輯的製作過程，並分享了對自身活動的想法。

               對我來說的革命

——首先從年末的話題開始說起。參與【COUNTDOWN JAPAN 24/25】的舞台感受如何？

星街：這場演出跟我自己的演唱會不同，現場有許多可能不認識我的人，但他們依然非常熱情，讓我感到非常高興。我和樂團成員還說「我們大幹了一場呢」，演出結束後我也自搜了網上的評價，有人留言說「雖然以前只聽過名字，但這場演出真的很棒」。

——尤其是在您出演的最後一天，除了常見的搖滾樂團外，SixTONES 和 NewJeans 等多元的陣容也非常吸引人。觀眾群體應該相當廣泛，您是怎麼考慮如何展現自我的呢？

星街：雖然作為 VTuber 是虛擬的存在，但其實我們也是和大家一樣的「人」，我覺得這次可能成功地讓觀眾感受到這一點。另外，演出前我也進行了公開彩排。

——這確實是音樂節特有的形式呢。

星街：我還認真帶動了現場的應援互動，也努力讓大家感受到我們的熱情。

——考慮到這場演出緊接著巡演，是否也因此狀態調整得更好呢？

星街：是的，因為巡演剛好在三個地點舉行了演出，累積了經驗，所以能帶著「好，衝吧！」的心情參加這次活動。如果去年完全沒有演唱會經驗，我可能會非常緊張，但因為巡演結束後我的狀態非常好，這次也能以良好的熱情投入其中。

——經歷了這樣的年末活動後，您推出了備受期待的新專輯《新星目錄》。您的首張專輯主打「彗星般閃耀的明星原石」，展現了偶像般閃亮的新鮮感；第二張專輯則將活動中的煩惱和掙扎昇華為作品。那麼，第三張專輯對您來說是怎樣的一張作品呢？

星街：我們團隊對專輯的風格有簡單的定義，第一張是「閃亮」，第二張是「閃耀」。接下來我們討論第三張時，決定「那就爆炸吧！」於是出現了「創造新時代」的概念，並以「革命」作為主題。作為虛擬藝術家，目前我們在社會中還是一個異質的存在，還未被視為真正的人。但我想表達的是，我們是真正在唱歌、跳舞的，而這就是我心中的革命。因此，專輯中收錄了許多表達這種目標的歌曲。

——從「閃亮」、「閃耀」到「爆發」。武道館公演的主題也是“SuperNova（超新星）”。至於專輯名中的「目錄」，是否帶有某種自我介紹的意涵？

星街：原本我們計劃只用「新星」這個詞，但當我們看到 Mika Pikazo 老師設計的專輯封面時，覺得畫作非常美，我們想在不妨礙設計的情況下加上文字，於是決定放在四角，並加入了「目錄」這個詞。雖然當時並沒有特別深的含義，但之後大家給出了很多很棒的解讀，那就這麼定了（笑）。

——也就是說，專輯名稱是在最後才決定的？

星街：沒錯，是在收到封面設計之後才定下來的。不過「新星」這個詞是我從一開始就想使用的。

——您過去在配信和訪談中多次提到：「希望 VTuber 能更廣泛地被社會接受，所以自己也會不斷挑戰。」這次更是將這一理念明確作為主題進行創作。您在製作過程中具體考慮了哪些方面呢？

星街：在第二張專輯中，我已經展現了不少鬱結、混沌的情感，但我希望在此基礎上進一步進化。所以在第二次個人演唱會結束後，我開始思考如何展現更加進化的樣子。這個階段就是要展現新的挑戰與突破，我認為現在正是這樣的階段。

（Part 2 待續。）

Billboard JAPAN

<Interview> Aiming for a New Era—
Hololive Virtual Idol Hoshimachi Suisei Sings
“Revolution” in Her Music

January 2025

Interviewed by : Takuto Ueda

Hoshimachi Suisei, a VTuber and virtual idol under Hololive, has released her new album,《Shinsei Mokuroku》.

This is her third album and her first in about two years since her previous work, 《Specter》. The album is an ambitious project centered around the keyword “revolution.” It includes 11 tracks created by a diverse and talented lineup of creators, such as the rising VOCALOID producer Tsumiki, whose track “Bibbidiba” became her first to surpass 100 million total streams. Other contributors include Soichiro Yamauchi (Fujifabric), Enon Kawatani (indigo la End, Gesu no Kiwami Otome, etc.), Deu (PEOPLE 1), Natori, and Haruno. Hoshimachi Suisei herself takes on songwriting and composition for the first time with the closing track, “Kireigoto”.

Hoshimachi Suisei has achieved numerous “Firsts” in VTuber history. With a long-held desire to make VTubers more recognized in society, she has poured her determination to forge a new era into this third album. On February 1st, she will fulfill her dream of holding a solo concert at Japan’s iconic Nippon Budokan. On the brink of this major turning point, she reflects on the album’s creation process and shares her thoughts on her career.

         My Revolution

—Let’s start with your recent performance at 【COUNTDOWN JAPAN 24/25】. How was the experience?

Hoshimachi: Unlike my own live shows, I imagine there were a lot of people in the audience who didn’t know me, but the energy was amazing, and I was really happy. My band members and I even said to each other, “We nailed it!” After the performance, I checked social media and saw comments like, “I only knew her name, but that was great!”

—Especially on the final day of the festival, the lineup was quite diverse, featuring regular rock bands alongside SixTONES and NewJeans. The audience must have been very diversified. How did you plan to present yourself?

Hoshimachi: Although I’m a VTuber and exist in a virtual space, I wanted to convey that I’m just like everyone else—a human being. I think I managed to achieve that. They even let me do an open rehearsal before the main show.

—That’s a very festival-like feature.

Hoshimachi: I made sure to encourage call-and-response interactions and tried to create a real sense of shared energy.

—Coming right after your tour, your condition must have been well-prepared for this performance, correct?

Hoshimachi: Yes, since I had just completed a three-show tour, I had the experience under my belt and felt like, “Let’s do this!” If I hadn’t done any live shows last year, I probably would have been super nervous. But coming off the tour, I could bring great energy into this performance.

—After such a busy year-end, you’ve now released your much-anticipated new album, Shinsei Mokuroku. With your debut album emphasizing the “fresh, sparkly feeling of a shooting star” and your second album expressing struggles and emotions through your activities, how would you describe this third album?

Hoshimachi: Within the team, we referred to the first album as “sparkle,” the second as “shiny,” and for the third, we thought, “What’s next? How about an explosion?” From there, the concept evolved into “let’s create a new era,” leading to the theme of “revolution.” As a virtual artist, I feel like we’re still seen as an unusual presence in society—not entirely recognized as human. But the fact is, I sing and dance myself, and making people understand that is my revolution. That’s the kind of message I aimed to deliver through this album.

—From “sparkle” to “shine” to an “explosion.” The title of your Budokan performance, “SuperNova,” fits perfectly with that progression. As for the term “Mokuroku” (Catalogue) in the album title, does it carry a self-introductory nuance?

Hoshimachi: Initially, we were just going to use “Shinsei” (Nova), but Mika Pikazo-sensei’s jacket illustration was so beautiful that I wanted to add some text in a way that wouldn’t interfere with the artwork. That’s how “Mokuroku” (Catalogue) was added. It didn’t have a deep meaning at first, but since people have interpreted it in such wonderful ways, I’ll go with that (laughs).

—So the title was finalized just last minute?

Hoshimachi: Yes, after the jacket art arrived. I was always determined to use the term “Shinsei” (Nova), though.

—In past streams and interviews, you’ve frequently mentioned your desire for VTubers to gain wider societal acceptance and your commitment to taking on challenges to achieve that. This time, you’ve made it the direct theme of your album. What were your specific thoughts during the production process?

Hoshimachi: With my second album, I showed a lot of darker, more turbulent emotions. But after that, I felt like I needed to close that chapter and show a more evolved version of myself. Around the time my second solo concert ended, I started thinking about how to demonstrate that growth. I realized it was time to showcase new challenges and breakthroughs—this album is about that next phase.

(Continues on Part 2.)

As soon as 🌸 heard that, she excitedly shouted, “Yakiniku!”

title: Real Sound 星街彗星專訪 Part 3 星街彗星對日本的攻略度是……？ ——在巡演首日，2025年的計劃也隨之公佈。首先是第三張原創全專輯《新星目錄》將於1月22日發行。…
context:
Real Sound 星街彗星專訪

Part 3

星街彗星對日本的攻略度是……？

——在巡演首日，2025年的計劃也隨之公佈。首先是第三張原創全專輯《新星目錄》將於1月22日發行。

星街：就像之前的專輯一樣，在專輯送到大家手中並收到反應之前，我都會一直抱著「真的沒問題嗎……」的那種不安（笑）。不過，這次的作品真的完成得非常棒！第一張專輯是「閃亮」，第二張專輯是「閃耀」，所以到了第三張我自己也在苦惱：「那麼第三張該怎麼表現呢？」結果，我決定這次就「爆發」吧（笑）。我一直有一種強烈的意願，想要不斷開創新的時代，因此以「革命」為概念，突破自我，展示更成長的星街彗星，並嘗試了許多以前從未挑戰過的歌曲。同時，我也邀請了許多創作者參與製作，從這個意義上來說，這是一張具革命性意義的專輯。

——帶著這張專輯，2月1日將舉辦首次的日本武道館公演《SUPERNOVA》。這個從出道開始就公開表示是夢想的舞台，終於即將站上去了。

星街：在埼玉超級競技場宣佈這消息的時候，很多粉絲高興得哭了，我自己也非常開心。從一開始我就一直說「目標是日本武道館！」，一路努力到了今天，這場演唱會對星街彗星的人生來說，真的是非常重要的里程碑。說實話，將武道館作為夢想有點像一種豪言壯語，但我一直認為，目標越大，實現時的感動就越大（笑）。而現在這個夢想真的實現了！那些從以前就支持我的粉絲也說：「沒想到真的走到了這一步啊」（笑）。我希望在當天能夠和大家一同分享這些感受，盡情享受這一刻。

——成功舉辦武道館公演後，這應該會成為向未來邁進的重要一步吧？

星街：是的。坦白說，當決定能在武道館舉辦演唱會時，我心裡也有些忐忑：「這樣真的可以嗎？」我擔心一直以來追求的夢想實現後，我的故事會完美收尾，然後失去繼續前進的動力。所以我一度想過，也許不去實現這個夢想反而更好。

——但最終，您還是選擇了實現這個夢想。

星街：是的。畢竟，若是讓其他人先在武道館開唱，我會感到不甘心（笑）。所以我認為，作為Hololive第一位登上武道館的成員，我應該留下足跡。另外，我最大的目標是將VTuber推廣到每家每戶中。所以在實現武道館的夢想後，我相信自己還能繼續朝著這個最終目標堅定地邁進。

——也就是說，登上武道館並不是您活動的最終目的。

星街：沒錯。創造並展示未來的藍圖才是最重要的。因此，在武道館之後，我也會繼續展開活動，用行動傳達「故事還沒有結束」的意志，現在也在籌劃許多新的計劃。星街彗星會繼續向前邁進！

——2025年，大家也期待您能登上《NHK紅白歌合戰》的舞台。

星街：《紅白》是我活動中想要實現的目標之一。2024年因為《ビビデバ》的成功，我和工作人員都抱著「一定要登上紅白！」的決心努力著，但最終還是未能實現……不過說實話，我心裡也鬆了一口氣。巡演圓滿完成，武道館也定下了，第三張專輯也將發行。如果再加上《紅白》，夢想就實現得太多了，感覺下一步反而會迷茫（笑）。所以我想今年再努力，創作出超越《ビビデバ》的作品。

——我們非常期待您今年的精彩表現！最後請問，去年年初的訪談中，您曾提到2023年對日本的攻略度，當時您是怎麼評估的？

星街：啊，是有這麼回事。我當時說了幾％來著（笑）？

——去年您說是20％。經歷了2024年後，現在的攻略度是多少呢？

星街：嗯……那就39％吧。如果沒有《ビビデバ》的成功，大概會是23％吧（笑）。

——比起2023年，幾乎翻了一倍呢。

星街：一年提升19％，真的很厲害吧（笑）。接下來我會一步步努力提升，讓數值突破50％，2025年也請多多支持！

（全文完）

Real Sound Hoshimachi Suisei Interview

Part 3

How much progress has Hoshimachi Suisei made in conquering Japan?

— On the first day of the tour, plans for 2025 were announced. First, the third original full album, Shinsei Mokuroku, will be released on January 22.

Suisei: Just like with my previous albums, until they actually reach everyone and I see their reactions, I spend my time feeling a bit anxious, wondering, “Is this okay…?” (laughs). But it’s turned out to be an amazing piece of work! The first album was themed around “sparkle,” the second was “shine,” so I really thought hard about what the theme for the third one should be. In the end, I decided to “explode” this time (laughs). I have a strong desire to constantly pave the way for new eras, so I adopted “revolution” as the concept. With this in mind, I aimed to break through yet another shell and create a collection of songs that showcases a more mature version of Hoshimachi Suisei. I worked on tracks that I hadn’t attempted before and collaborated with a variety of artists. In that sense, I believe this is truly a revolutionary album.

— Following the release of this album, on February 1, you’ll be holding your first concert at the Nippon Budokan, SUPERNOVA. Finally, you’re stepping onto the dream stage you’ve been talking about since your debut.

Suisei: When I announced it at the Saitama Super Arena, so many fans cried in tears of joy. I was incredibly happy as well. From the very beginning, I’ve been saying, “I’m aiming for the Nippon Budokan!” and I’ve come this far with that goal in mind. This concert will truly be a significant event in the life of Hoshimachi Suisei. Honestly, declaring Budokan as my dream was kind of a “big ego” moment. I figured that if the goal was incredibly big, the emotional impact of achieving it would be even greater (laughs). And now it’s actually happening! Even fans who’ve supported me from the early days have said, “I never imagined you’d come this far” (laughs). I want to share those feelings with everyone and just enjoy the day to its fullest.

— If you succeed with the Budokan live, it will surely be a major stepping stone toward your future, right?

Suisei: That’s right. To be honest, when it was decided that I could perform at the Budokan, I did wonder, “Is this really okay?” I worried that achieving this long-standing dream might wrap up my story too neatly and leave me feeling burnt out. I even thought that maybe it would be better not to achieve the dream of Budokan at all.

— But in the end, you chose to realize that dream.

Suisei: Yes. After all, I’d feel frustrated if someone else performed at the Budokan first (laughs). I thought it would be better to leave my mark there as the first member of Hololive. Plus, my ultimate goal, the future I want to achieve, is to bring VTubers more into mainstream households. So after fulfilling the dream of performing at the Budokan, I felt I could continue to move powerfully toward that ultimate goal.

— So performing at the Budokan isn’t the ultimate purpose of your activities, is it?

Suisei: Exactly. Creating and showing what’s beyond that is the most important part. That’s why even after Budokan, I’m planning various activities to firmly demonstrate the message that “the story continues.” I want Hoshimachi Suisei to keep moving forward!

— We’re also hoping to see you appear on NHK’s Kohaku Uta Gassen in 2025.

Suisei: Appearing on Kohaku is one of the goals I want to achieve in my activities. In 2024, with the success of “BIBBIDIBA” my team and I worked really hard with the mindset of “We want to make it to Kohaku!”, but unfortunately, we didn’t make it… That said, I feel a bit relieved as well. With the tour completed, the Budokan concert secured, and the third album coming out, if we had also made it to Kohaku, it would’ve felt like all my dreams had come true too quickly, leaving me wondering what to aim for next (laughs). I want to keep working hard next year to create something even greater than “BIBBIDIBA”

— We’re looking forward to your remarkable progress this year! Lastly, in an interview published at the beginning of last year, you mentioned your “conquest level” of Japan in 2023.

Suisei: Oh, right, I did say something about that. How many percent did I say again? (laughs)

— Last year, you said 20%. How would you evaluate your current level after 2024?

Suisei: Hmm… let’s say 39%. Without the success of BIBBIDIBA, it probably would’ve been around 23% (laughs).

— It nearly doubled compare to 2023.

Suisei: A 19% increase in one year is pretty impressive, right? (laughs) From here on, I want to keep steadily increasing that percentage, aiming to surpass the 50% mark. I’ll work hard in 2025 as well, so please continue to support me!

(This concludes the interview.)Real Sound 星街彗星專訪

Part 2

從街頭演唱到SSA公演
「希望我的每一步都能讓其他人跟隨」

——即使起點不同，最終還是希望大家能一樣喜歡上音樂和配信，是這樣的想法嗎？

星街：這個嘛……在粉絲中也有只對配信感興趣的人。最近因為太忙，完全無法配信，真的很抱歉（笑）。但我覺得這樣也沒問題。只要能對星街彗星產生興趣，對我來說就是值得高興的事情。所以我希望大家可以按照自己喜歡的方式來享受，這樣就很好了。

——《ビビデバ》的熱潮之後，去年也能在各種電視節目中看到您的身影。您已經連續兩年出演了《THE MUSIC DAY》（日本電視台）。

星街：真的非常感激。去年是第二次出演，我演唱了《ソワレ》，而且當時AKB48的成員還一起伴舞。能和我一直以來都認識的超級偶像們合作，真的是一次非常棒的經驗。

——隨著活動的展開，與現實中的音樂人互動的機會也越來越多。去年您也參加了《SUKIMASWITCH》的致敬專輯。

星街：這是一件非常光榮的事情。作為VTuber，踏入從未有人涉足的領域對我來說是件非常有趣的事。所以每次都會帶著「太棒了！這是沒人做過的第一步！」的心情，盡情享受每件事情。雖然有很多事情都掛上了“VTuber初次”這樣的頭銜，也因此聽到了很多不同的聲音，但我希望能為那些會接續這些第一步的人們開闢更多的道路。

——還是會感受到社會對VTuber的偏見嗎？

星街：嗯，的確還是會有。我覺得很多發表負面言論的人，是因為對VTuber的理解還不夠深入。因此，我希望能繼續努力提高大家的認識度。就像是在說「吃吧，吃吧！」一樣，讓大家感受到VTuber的美好和有趣之處（笑）。

——與其為負面反應而感到憂慮，不如從未開的領域中挖掘出更多可能性。

星街：沒錯。像我現在能夠參與各種電視節目，也是因為電視相關從業人員對VTuber的理解逐漸加深了。所以，只要我繼續進行各種活動，從身邊的地方開始，情況就會慢慢改變，進而提升大家對VTuber的認識。

——或許通過您在2024年的活動，已經有人對VTuber的偏見消除了。

星街：嗯，確實如此。《ビビデバ》的留言區中出現了好幾百條類似「原本對VTuber沒什麼好印象，但聽了這首歌後覺得很好」的評論。我覺得這是個非常好的趨勢，希望能將因此誕生的聯繫再進一步擴大。

——去年9月您還在澀谷舉行了街頭演唱，真的很驚訝。

星街：呵呵呵呵。我當時一直說「我想做，我想做！」，最終硬是說服了工作人員幫我實現這個夢想。真的非常有趣（笑）。

——很多人可能覺得「VTuber怎麼可能舉行街頭演唱？」。您當時就很篤定一定能實現嗎？

星街：嗯，我就覺得一定可以。雖然我不太懂技術，但我當時的想法就是「把螢幕放在那裡不就好了嗎？」（笑）。不過實際完成的街頭演唱設備，比我想像的要豪華得多，真的非常感謝那些幫我實現想法的大人們（笑）。

——當天在X有稍微的暗示，現場的觀眾以粉絲為主嗎？

星街：不，大多數人都是偶然路過停下來的。我問他們「知道星街彗星嗎？」時，他們都說「現在才知道啊」，只有少數幾個人本來就認識我。能當面看到那些不認識我的人的反應，真的是非常寶貴的經驗。如果還有機會的話，我也很想再次嘗試。我希望我的這一步，能讓更多人跟隨。如果有更多VTuber舉行街頭演唱，澀谷應該會變得很有趣（笑）。

——到處都擺著螢幕的景象（笑）。

星街：哈哈哈哈，那肯定非常有意思（笑）。

——11月開始，您的首場巡演《Spectra of Nova》也正式啟動了。

星街：我的第一次（2021年的《STELLAR into the GALAXY》）和第二次（2023年的《Shout in Crisis》）演唱會，都是基於專輯製作的內容。但這次是首次巡演，所以把它設計成了過去活動的總集篇。這種全新的方式讓我也有些不安，「真的可以嗎？大家會喜歡嗎？」。但當正式開始後，每個會場都響起了熱烈的歡呼聲，我才放心下來。這次很多人都是第一次參加我的演唱會。

——我參加了首場埼玉超級競技場的演出，能感受到您的顯著進步。

星街：謝謝您。為了準備巡演，我回顧了第一次演唱會的影像，當時的表演讓我忍不住覺得「哇，真是青澀啊！」（笑）。所以在巡演中，我也懷著想展示自己進步的心情，不斷努力演唱和舞蹈。

——最近，兔田佩可拉和寶鐘瑪琳也舉辦了個人演唱會，這些成員的表現是否也給了您一些激勵？

星街：是的。現在，幾乎所有Hololive成員都以舉辦個人演唱會為目標努力著。比起擴大VTuber的影響力，他們更多的是為了回饋粉絲。看到他們一個接一個地實現夢想，我也非常感慨。同時，我也有一個很大膽的願望，希望自己作為第一個舉辦巡演和武道館演唱會的成員，能成為大家的榜樣。我希望我的演唱會能感動觀眾，並將這種情感傳遞給其他成員。這對於我來說，是一個非常大的動力來源。

Real Sound Hoshimachi Suisei Interview

Part 2

From Street Performances to SSA Concerts: “I Want Others to Follow My Steps”

–– Even if the starting points are different, do you hope that in the end, people will love both your music and your streams equally?

Suisei: Hmm, I’m not sure. Some fans are only interested in my streams. Lately, I’ve been so busy that I haven’t been able to stream at all, and I feel bad about that (laughs). But that’s totally fine. I’m happy just knowing that people are interested in Hoshimachi Suisei, so I think everyone should enjoy it in their own way, however they like.

–– Following the success of “Bibbidiba”, we also saw you on various TV shows last year. You even performed at The Music Day (Nippon TV) for the second year in a row.

Suisei: I’m really grateful for that. Last year, I performed “Soiree” for my second appearance, and AKB48 members danced alongside me during the performance. Collaborating with such legendary super idols, whom I’ve known about for a long time, was an amazing experience.

–– Over time, your interactions with real-life artists have increased. You even participated in SUKIMASWITCH’s tribute album last year.

Suisei: That was such an honor. As a VTuber, I enjoy stepping into areas no one has ventured into before. Every time, I get excited thinking, “Yes! I get to take the first step into uncharted territory!” It’s so much fun. Being the “first VTuber” to do something often brings a lot of attention, including criticism, but I see it as paving the way for others. I hope the paths I create become steps that others can follow.

–– Do you still feel a lot of prejudice toward VTubers?

Suisei: Yes, definitely. Most of the negative comments come from people who have a low “resolution” of understanding when it comes to VTubers. That’s why I want to work hard to raise that understanding. I want to feed people the best parts of VTubers, saying, “Try it! It’s good!” (laughs).

–– Instead of being disheartened by negative reactions, it’s better to see potential in unexplored areas, isn’t it?

Suisei: Exactly. The reason I’ve been able to appear on TV so much recently is that the people in the industry have come to better understand VTubers. If I keep engaging in various activities, I believe the situation will continue to improve. By doing so, I think people’s perceptions of VTubers will naturally become more positive over time.

–– Your activities in 2024 may have already changed how some people view VTubers.

Suisei: Yes, definitely. For example, in the comment section of “Bibbidiba,” I saw hundreds of comments saying things like, “I never thought positively about VTubers before, but after hearing this song, I was blown away.” That kind of feedback is a great trend, and I hope to expand that ripple effect even further.

–– In September, you even did a street performance in Shibuya, which surprised many people.

Suisei: Hehehe. I kept insisting to the staff, “I really want to do this! Please make it happen!” And they granted my wish. It was so much fun (laughs).

–– It’s easy to assume, “VTubers can’t do street performances,” but did you have confidence that it was possible?

Suisei: Yes, I was sure it was doable. I’m not great with tech, but I just thought, “We’ll just put up a screen, right?” (laughs). But the actual street performance setup turned out to be much more elaborate than I had imagined. I’m grateful to the team for expanding on my little idea (laughs).

–– On the day of the street performance, there was a small hint about it on X (formerly Twitter). Was the audience mostly made up of fans?

Suisei: No, most of the audience were people who just happened to pass by and stopped to watch. When I asked, “Do you know who Hoshimachi Suisei is?” most people said, “I just found out about you now.” Only a handful of people already knew me. Seeing the reactions of people who didn’t know me in real-time was such a valuable experience. I’d love to do it again if I get the chance. I also hope other VTubers follow this—it would make Shibuya such a fun place (laughs).

–– With screens set up everywhere, it could get wild (laughs).

Suisei: Hahaha, that would be hilarious (laughs).

–– In November, you embarked on your first-ever tour, Spectra of Nova. How did it feel?

Suisei: My first live (Stellar into the Galaxy, held in 2021) and second live (Shout in Crisis, held in 2023) were both created around the concept of their respective albums. But since this was my first tour, I structured it as a sort of “greatest hits” compilation. It was a different way of planning a show, so I was nervous, wondering, “Will people enjoy it?” But once the tour started, the cheers from the audience at every venue reassured me. I also noticed many people attending a Suisei live for the first time, which made me really happy.

–– I attended the first show at Saitama Super Arena, and I was struck by how much you’ve evolved as a performer.

Suisei: Thank you! While preparing for the tour, I rewatched footage of my first live, and I couldn’t help but think, “Wow, I was so inexperienced!” (laughs). So for the tour, I was determined to showcase my growth, singing and dancing with that goal in mind.

–– Recently, other Hololive members like Usada Pekora and Houshou Marine have also been hosting solo arena concerts. Do their achievements inspire you?

Suisei: Absolutely. Most Hololive talents aim to hold their own solo concerts. For us, it’s more than just spreading the word about VTubers—it’s about giving back to our fans. Seeing everyone’s dreams come true, one step at a time, is incredibly moving. That said, I’ll be bold here: I want others to see me as the benchmark for tours and big venues like Budokan. I pour my heart into creating live performances that move people, and I want other talents to experience that same passion. It’s a huge
motivation for me as I continue to perform.

(Continues on Part 3.)

經歷《ビビデバ》大熱之後，立志在2025年迎來更大飛躍

2025.01.01 13:00

Real Sound 星街彗星專訪

Part 1

2024年，星街彗星在音樂界再次展現了強烈的存在感。不僅3月發行的《ビビデバ》創下了總播放數超過1億次的爆紅紀錄，還首次舉辦了從11月到12月巡迴3個城市（包括埼玉超級競技場）的演唱會，其成績與規模均超越以往，展現出更加卓越的表現。

《Real Sound》特地對這樣的星街彗星進行了回顧2024年的專訪。在2024年1月1日刊登的採訪中，她曾表示日本的攻略程度只有「20%」。然而，經過去年的活動後，這個數字又提升到了多少呢？請來確認答案吧！（編輯部）

2024年真的是「忙到不行（笑）」。

——2023年之後，對星街小姐來說，2024年應該是再次大幅躍進的一年。您自己感覺度過了怎樣的一年呢？

星街彗星（以下簡稱星街）： 正如您所說，我也覺得這確實是一個躍進的一年。而「ビビデバ」能大受歡迎，真的起到了非常大的作用。我很深刻地感受到，這首歌傳達到了那些不知道 VTuber 是什麼的人手中。很多人因為對這首歌感興趣，後來才發現「這是 VTuber 唱的啊」，這種現象真的發生了很多。這不僅讓更多人了解了這首歌，還形成了「那我也來聽聽其他 VTuber 的歌吧」這樣的連鎖效應。我覺得這對我自己，對整個虛擬偶像業界來說，都是一件好事。

——您去年曾在採訪中提到「希望2024年能稍微休息一下，在不太累的狀態下找到平衡」，但實際上似乎非常忙碌呢。

星街： 真的太忙了（笑）。今年我也想稍微休息一下，慢慢進行活動，但每次我在配信中這麼說，就會收到一堆「又來了，你不可能做到吧」這樣的留言（笑）。

——這種忙碌其實也是來自大家對您的期待吧。您應該也感到很有成就感吧？

星街： 當然了！雖然我會有「啊，太忙了，好辛苦啊！」的感覺，但每一個邀約都讓我感到很開心，每一件事都是我想做的。其實並沒有什麼是不想做的工作，所以才會覺得雖然很辛苦，但也充滿了喜悅。

——4月時您稍微休息了一下，那段時間有好好放鬆嗎？

星街： 非常放鬆！當時「ビビデバ」的播放數正在迅速上升，利用那段時間我也思考了「接下來該怎麼做？」、「下一首歌該如何計劃？」雖然說是休假，但其實也算是一直在想工作的事情（笑）。不過那段時間我回了老家，也玩得很開心，做了很多新嘗試。這一年我也想再安排一個月的假期（笑）。

——接下來想請您談談去年的一些重要話題，首先當然是「ビビデバ」的成功。當歌曲完成時，您是否感到很有信心？

星街： 為我創作「ビビデバ」的ツミキ先生，其實也是我翻唱歌曲中最受歡迎的「フォニイ」的原作者。所以從一開始，我就確信ツミキ先生創作的歌曲一定會很棒。而完成後，這首歌果然非常時尚、洗腦，我自己也很喜歡這首歌。接下來的挑戰是如何讓這首歌流行起來。我嘗試了很多方法，特別加強了短影音的推廣，結果真的觸及到了很多人。我很喜歡自己的每一首歌曲，但這次我特別努力地讓更多不認識星街彗星的人接觸到它。

——話題性的MV似乎對歌曲的成功也有很大影響。

星街： 沒錯。擬態するメタ先生提出了一個非常棒的點子，製作出了一個很有趣的 MV。我一直很希望能請他來幫忙製作 MV，這次能在「ビビデバ」成功合作，真的很開心。我只簡單說了一下歌曲的主題，其他部分都交給他發揮，結果做出了讓很多人覺得有趣、引人注目的作品，真的很感謝。尤其是扔鞋的那個場景，超級火（笑）。

——「ビビデバ」上線僅兩週就突破了1000萬次播放，11月13日更是達成1億次播放。
星街： 坦白說，第一波數字激增之後，我就覺得有點像是它自己在成長（笑）。

——就像歌曲自己開始走向世界一樣。

星街： 沒錯，感覺像是「啊，這裡也被用到了！」，但我自己忙得不可開交，幾乎沒時間去研究哪邊又提到這首歌了（笑）。等我注意到時已經是「哇，8000萬了！」「9000萬了！」最後「1億了！」但這種情況其實很好，因為歌曲已經擴展到了我無法覆蓋的範圍，這是很了不起的事情，我非常開心。

——對於1億次播放，您能感受到它的意義嗎？

星街： 說實話，還是很難具體感受到（笑）。從文字上看1億次當然很厲害，但實際感覺還是模糊的。不過，這確實讓我有了「下一首也要做到1億次播放」的想法。

——「ビビデバ」的成功是否讓頻道訂閱數增加，或吸引更多人觀看您的配信？

星街： 訂閱數確實大幅增長了，但也有很多人其實只聽過歌，從未看過我的配信。對我來說，這反而是件開心的事。當然，如果也看配信我會很高興，但即使只是聽歌並成為粉絲，這對我來說已經是一大步了。VTuber 的模式通常是通過配信吸引觀眾，但如果有人是通過音樂認識我們，那也完全沒有問題。

（Part 2待續）

Hoshimachi Suisei : “I need to create another song that can reach 100 million views”

Pledging further growth in 2025 following the massive success of “BIBBIDIBA”

Real Sound Hoshimachi Suisei Interview

January 1st, 2025  13:00

Part 1

In 2024, Hoshimachi Suisei continued to make her mark in the music scene. Her March 2024 release, “ビビデバ” (BIBBIDIBA), became a viral hit, surpassing 100 million total streams. Additionally, she held her first-ever tour from November to December, covering three cities, including the Saitama Super Arena. Both her records and the scale of her activities exceeded those of previous years, showcasing remarkable achievements.

Real Sound conducted an interview with Hoshimachi Suisei to reflect on her 2024. In an interview published on January 1, 2024, she described her progress in “conquering Japan” as only 20%. However, with her achievements from the past year, how much has that percentage increased? Be sure to check her answer. (Editorial team)

Suisei described 2024 as “an incredibly hectic year (laughs).”

Interviewer: Continuing from 2023, 2024 was another year of significant growth for you, Hoshimachi-san. How would you describe the year from your perspective?

Hoshimachi Suisei (hereafter, Suisei): As you said, I do feel it was a year of great progress for me. The huge success of “ビビデバ” (BIBBIDIBA) was especially impactful. I really felt the song reached and resonated with people who didn’t previously know about VTubers. There were so many cases where people got interested in the song itself and later realized, “Oh, this is sung by a VTuber.” It even sparked a chain reaction of people thinking, “Maybe I’ll check out other VTuber songs too.” I think that was not only great for me but also beneficial for the entire virtual industry.

Interviewer: In last year’s interview, you mentioned wanting to “take it slow in 2024, balancing work without pushing too hard.” But in reality, it seems you had a hectic schedule, right?

Suisei: It was way too busy (laughs). This year, I’d like to take it easy and work at a slower pace. But whenever I say that during a stream, I get a flood of comments like, “There she goes again. Yeah, right” (laughs).

Interviewer: That kind of busyness is proof of how much demand there is for you. Does that bring you a sense of fulfillment?

Suisei: Absolutely. Even though I often feel, “I’m so busy! This is tough!” every opportunity I receive is something I’m genuinely happy about and want to take on. There isn’t a single job I don’t want to do. It’s a rewarding kind of challenge—a happy kind of exhaustion, you could say.

Interviewer: You did manage to take a short break in April. Were you able to refresh yourself during that time?

Suisei: I really did. At that time, BIBBIDIBA had just been released and its numbers were skyrocketing, so during the break, I thought a lot about what to do next and what kind of song to release afterward. In that sense, it wasn’t a completely work-free vacation (laughs). But I did go back to my family home and had a ton of fun. I got to try a lot of new things and gather inspiration. I’d like to take a similar one-month vacation this year too (laughs).

Interviewer: Let’s dive into the major highlights of last year. The success of Bibideba is something we can’t skip. Did you feel a strong sense of potential when the song was completed?

Suisei: The composer, Tsumiki-san, also created Phony, which is the most popular cover song I’ve posted. So, in that context, I was sure anything created with Tsumiki-san’s talent would turn out amazing. When BIBBIDIBA was finished, it became such a catchy and stylish song—one that I personally love. After that, it was all about figuring out how to make it go viral. I experimented a lot, especially focusing on short video approaches, which ultimately helped the song reach a wider audience. I love all my songs, but this time, I worked particularly hard to ensure the music reached people who didn’t know about Hoshimachi Suisei.

Interviewer: The music video, which garnered a lot of attention, also seemed to play a significant role in the song’s success.

Suisei: Absolutely. Gitai Suru Meta-san came up with truly incredible ideas and created such an engaging MV. I’d been wanting to work with Gitai Suru Meta-san for a while, and I was thrilled we could collaborate on BIBBIDIBA. I just shared the general theme of the song and left the rest to them, and they delivered an MV that so many people found fun and captivating. The shoe-throwing scene became especially popular (laughs).

Interviewer: BIBBIDIBA surpassed 10 million streams within about two weeks of its release and continued growing, hitting 100 million on November 13.

Suisei: Honestly, after the initial surge, it felt like the song took on a life of its own. It kept growing in ways I wasn’t directly involved in.

Interviewer: Like the song started spreading on its own?

Suisei: Exactly. I’d see it being used in places I didn’t expect, and I could barely keep up with its momentum. I was so busy that I didn’t even have much time to search for mentions online (laughs). It was more like, “Oh, it’s at 80 million! Now it’s 90 million! Wow, it hit 100 million!” Even so, I felt it was a great thing that the song reached places I couldn’t personally oversee. It’s amazing that it was recognized and appreciated by so many people. I was genuinely happy.

Interviewer: Does the figure of 100 million streams feel real to you?

Suisei: Honestly, not really (laughs). Seeing the number “100 million” written down, I know it’s an impressive achievement, but it doesn’t feel very tangible. However, it has motivated me to create another song that could reach 100 million streams.

Interviewer: Did BIBBIDIBA’s success bring an increase in your channel subscribers or stream viewers?

Suisei: My channel subscribers did spike significantly. On the other hand, I noticed there were also many people who had never watched a Hoshimachi Suisei stream before. I actually found that exciting. Of course, I’d be happy if they watched my streams, but even if they only liked my music, that’s still a huge step forward. VTubers are often seen as streaming-centric, but there’s no rule that people can’t start as music fans and engage from there.

(Continues on Part 2.)

context:
昨日兩人的配信很多交叉內容所以直接合併整理：

-出場順序，像是Solo Part🌽🌸☄️的順序其實都是營運決定的。🌸聽到後非常開心的傳訊息給☄️。
-因為☄️最近太忙所以一直到前兩天才決定主持環節要寫信。還緊急請姐街把信紙印出來然後當天下午才偷偷帶到休息室寫完。
-由於現場配信時都穿著動補衣所以身上沒有口袋可以放信，最後放在了腰帶裡，結果信拿給AZKi時都皺皺的，還帶著自己的體溫。
-☄️回到後台時🌸哭著過來抱☄️還邊打著☄️說笨蛋、笨蛋。
-一開始🌽還沒有哭，但後來聽到AZKi說沒有畢業真是太好了直接破防。
-Fes結束後🌸☄️兩人是一起回家的。
-🌽🌸都被請去住酒店了，麻內們知道大家的房號以防有人睡過頭時可以直接去叫人。
-🌸晚上睡不著有傳Line給🌽問她要不要過來自己房間，結果🌽先睡了沒回應（還是說她不敢回應呢⋯）
-隔天早上🌸手機沒充到電但幸好有在該起來的時候醒過來，🌽也有傳Line 叫她。
-最近🌽🌸☄️這三人幾乎天天在一起。
-🌸改開台時間是因為要開會，而且是全部零期生的會議。
-☄️的Newton MV製作中。
-☄️想要有自己的Expo。
-成員們在後台看直播時都在找女粉，只要有自己的女粉出現大家就都會很興奮。
-☄️知道自己是壓軸後覺得壓力很大。
-成員們在後台待機時有玩撲克牌，🌸玩的時候還作弊。
-🌸很尊敬🌽對Hololive的愛。
-🌸發現☄️改了Last Frontier歌詞時又爆哭。
-在EXPO開始前成員們有先逛一次會場的機會，由工作人員帶領她們並且有分組，🌸☄️🔥🐑一組，🔥🐑很乖但🌸☄️就很興奮到處亂跑還帶著自己的娃娃到處拍照。
-試吃環節🌸選了商業套餐，☄️選了SMOK的餐點，🌸很生氣的問☄️為什麼不選商業套餐，☄️回答因為妳會分我，這樣我們就會一起吃那一份了。
-原本營運設計的商業餐是甜點，後來🌸☄️怕太甜不妥所以改漢堡了。
-🍃毫不意外的選了商業套餐，拿到mc卡後🌸☄️幫她簽了名。🍃不只是星詠她現在也是堅定的mcmt推。
-🌸☄️看到那個mcmt左右半心的也問營運說這真的沒問題嗎，不過這個最終被保留。
-表演當天的員工餐是Buffet，☄️真的就狂夾肉一點蔬菜都沒拿。
-3月24日火建有連動還會有公布。
-🌸也很想辦自己的Solo Live，最近也很努力的在連續發歌。
-🌸表示今天沒辦法來的及唸完所有的SC很抱歉，明天開始會恢復正常配信，還有希望大家在鯛魚燒活動結束前多去吃一些。

如果妳喜歡miComet，「好狐」 白上  吹雪🌽是一個妳絕對要認識的人物。即便不談🌽跟🌸☄️的關係，她本身也是一位SSSSSR+級的神V。🌸說過🌽是聖人般的存在。🌽幫助過的人無數。她本身就是一個創作能力很強的人，擅於想出各種有趣的節目企劃，臨場反應快，配合度高，又會製作，繪製各種素材，梗圖，迷因，短片，每天大量發推、轉推。但她對於幫助別人從不吝嗇才是重點，凡是有人缺上述資源的，配信需要連動的，來找🌽都有求必應。社內社外受過她幫助的人無數。無論誰只要談到🌽都是讚譽有加，號稱面子果實能力者。有無數的來自V界各方的證詞可以證明這一點。可以說（幾乎）是零負評人物。她也是龍心事件發生後，會長被炎上最嚴重的時期，唯一公開發推挺會長的人。這條推文作為重要的歷史文本至今還在，沒人能讓她刪文。可想而知這條推文下面是戰場。我之前說幾乎就是因為這樣：至今我唯一看過對🌽的負評就是來自小粉紅。理由也不需說明了。這事件要談下去篇幅極長，這也不是本篇重點，但我舉這個例子你就知道她的偉大。
即使這麼偉大的人也有脆弱需要人陪伴的時候。上次梅露事件中陪在🌽身邊最多的幾個人裡就有🌸☄️。小學堂那天🌸☄️也早到陪🌽。都說物以類聚，我相信像🌽這樣的好人會跟她好的也都是好人，這也是我自己喜歡mcmt的其中一個原因：這個世界上的好人真的不多。當然不是說其他人是壞人或🌽跟其他人感情就不好，不過🌸☄️🌽三人的頻率的同步率確實很高。這三人也都是自我要求很高的人，而且是利他主義者。FubumiComet的節目效果很好，但要看她們幾個感情實際上好不好的話要看她們私底下的互動。從她們幾個現在一天到晚出去吃飯，看電影，釣魚釣蝦，去主題餐廳，沒事就跑☄️家討論企劃，etc. 就不難看出她們的好交情。🌽也說感謝🌸☄️當她各種奇怪實驗企劃的白老鼠。☄️的整人企劃也交由🌸🌽執行。回到mcmt的愛情本身，聽聞有人會介意🌽是不是會變成mcmt中的第三者，連🌽本人都擔心有人會誤會。實在無需杞憂。因為🌽就不是這種人。她是mcmt近年最力推手。各種明戳暗戳，來自白上神父的各種關心，只差沒問🌸☄️什麼時候要生小孩了。🌽多次說過她是真正的mcmt派，會永遠守護miComet。我等mc民需要她的最近距離報導。
還有一點應該就是默契了，這裡我主要指發糖的默契，除了🌸☄️自己發的糖，品質最好最純的糖就是來自🌽。我觀察是因為🌸☄️也覺得有些糖由🌽來發更好，而且🌸☄️相信🌽在甜度上的拿捏。
這三人作為V界中的幾個最重要的先驅者之一，經歷過大小事件，不管在心境和經歷上都最了解彼此，她們是屬於她們這一代的。即便有一天她們不再做V了，這三人間的聯繫是不會斷的。
就像我前面說的，光🌽自己的配信的成績就有太多豐功偉業可說的，我也不太確定司空部對mcmt的看法為何，不過🌽在mc民這邊是推進🌸☄️感情非常重要的存在。有好狐真好。

A special existence in miComet🌸☄️:
Shirakami Fubuki🌽

If you are into miComet, then “Fine Fox” Shirakami Fubuki is a name you have to remember. Even without the relationship between🌽and🌸☄️, 🌽herself is already a SSSSSR+ grade Vtuber. 🌸once said🌽is a true saint. 🌽has helped countless people in the past. 🌽Herself is a very talented artist. She is good at planning streams, fast response in streams, and will cooperate to most requests. She creates all kinds of arts, memes and short films, she Tweets and Retweet a lot. However the most important thing is she will do her best to help those in need. Anyone needs any collaboration or the resources above, she will respond accordingly. People who have received her help are everywhere, from within or outside the company. People have nothing but compliments for🌽. She is sometimes called the one who has eaten the Fruit of Face, as a parody to the One Piece reference, which means everyone owns her a favor. There are tons of testimonies to prove that. She is(Almost)a person with no criticism against her. 🌽was the only person who tweeted in support of Kiryu Coco when Coco was suspended in the Taiwan incident. This tweet still exists as of today as an important piece of history, and no one would be able to ask her to delete it. Inevitably, the thread has became a battlefield. So that’s why I said almost. The only criticism I have ever seen against her were all from those Chinese mobs. And we all know the reason. This is a huge topic to get into, but that’s not the topic of this article. I mentioned this just to show you how majestic🌽is. Even a great person like her will have her fragile moments. When the Mel incident happened, 🌸☄️was among the people who stayed beside🌽the longest periods. The day they had the Elementary School Academic Assessment,🌸☄️arrived early to make sure🌽was alright. Birds of a feather flock together. I believe a good person like🌽would stick together with good people as well. That’s another reason why I like mcmt. Because there aren’t that many good people in the world. I am not saying that other people near them are bad, or🌸☄️🌽are not good friends with other people, but the trio do communicate on the same frequency more often compared to when they were talking to the others. The trio also had high expectations for themselves, and they are all altruists. FubumiComet creates great entertainment in their streams. But in order to see if they are true good friends you have to observe what they do off stream. They went out to eat together often, watch movies, fishing and shrimping, went to themed restaurants, and whenever they had a chance they would have meetings in☄️’s place to discuss stream plans. etc., one can easily tell🌸☄️🌽are good friends. 🌽said she was thankful for🌸☄️being her lab rats for all her bizarre experimental streams, and☄️’s prank stream was conducted under🌸🌽‘s help. Now back to the love between🌸☄️. I have heard people were worried that🌽becoming the third person. That is a baseless assumption. Because🌽is not that kind of person. She was actually the greatest assist in shipping🌸☄️. Great effort was made by🌽 in order to hint the couple to stay happily ever after. All the awareness that came from father Shirakami. 🌽is now in a state that she is about to ask🌸☄️when they are gonna have their first child. 🌽has stressed many times she is a mcmt believer and will guard them forever. We mcmt fans need her first hand journalism.
Another thing I am gonna mention here is about the trio have a tacit agreement. Here I mean when they were working on their sugar supplies. The best and purest sugar, besides what🌸☄️gave, were from🌽. My explanation for this is🌸☄️think some sugar is better delivered by🌽, and🌸☄️trust🌽for the right sweetness she should be given to us. The trio being some of the most important pioneers in the Vtuber field, they have been through lots of things. They understand each others very well as they came from a similar background and had similar experiences in the past. They are in a generation of their own. If, one day, the trio were no longer Vtubers, I do believe the connection between them will never be severed. As I stated above, 🌽is a great Vtuber herself, even if she’s had nothing to do with🌸☄️, her accomplishments as a Vtuber can never be ignored. I am not sure what Sukonbus think about miComet, but here in the world of mcmt, 🌽is considered as a great existence that propels the love between🌸☄️. Fine Fox is truly the finest of all.

title: Billboard JAPAN 2025年1月 星街彗星訪談 Part 3 會燃燒殆盡嗎？曾經也有這樣的不安 —— 在這部以「革命」為概念，描繪出柔韌且充滿力量的人物形象的專輯中，…
context:
Billboard JAPAN

2025年1月

星街彗星訪談

Part 3

會燃燒殆盡嗎？曾經也有這樣的不安

—— 在這部以「革命」為概念，描繪出柔韌且充滿力量的人物形象的專輯中，像《Caramel Pain》或《DEADPOOL feat. 花譜》這樣帶有陰鬱氛圍的世界觀，似乎顯得有些與眾不同。

星街： 我在創作過程中，是逐首歌曲慢慢對應的，最終整張專輯意外地統整得很好。《Caramel Pain》在討論會上其實只稍微聊了一點點，當時我還問「需要更多的資訊嗎？」但對方回答「也許隨意創作更能表現得好」。於是就交給他們發揮，結果完成的歌曲讓人覺得這首歌很有我的感覺，非常滿意。

—— 關於《DEADPOOL feat. 花譜》呢？

星街： 之前我和花譜醬在《一世風靡》這首歌中合作，那是一首可愛又流行的歌曲。但這次我想嘗試完全不同的風格，不太過於朗朗上口，也不追隨潮流，而是走向一個相反的方向來創作。雖然風格迥異，但這兩首歌都挑戰了許多新鮮的表達方式。

—— 所以並不是在考慮整張專輯的平衡性下來選曲的？

星街： 是的。真的是一首一首慢慢的做。其實第一張和第二張專輯也都是這樣，先做出自己想做的歌曲，然後再來思考整體時會懷疑「這樣真的能整合起來嗎？」結果完成後發現「成功了！」這樣的過程重複了三次。也多虧了創作者們對我的深刻理解，才讓專輯產生了連貫性，我非常感謝他們。

親自作詞作曲的初次挑戰：《綺麗事》

—— 這次專輯中還收錄了由星街自己作詞作曲的歌曲《綺麗事》。這是首次挑戰創作嗎？

星街： 是的，第一次。

—— 是什麼契機讓您開始創作的呢？

星街： 第二張專輯時我就想嘗試，但當時趕不上進度，或者說我無法下定決心去做。這次我說「第三張專輯一定要試試看」，於是逐步設定了截止日期……

—— 被外部壓力推動著完成了。

星街： 是啊，當時想「沒辦法了，只能做了」。雖然實際上好幾次超過了截止日期（笑），但總算是完成了。

—— 一開始設定的主題是什麼呢？

星街： 其實我腦海中有很多想做的歌曲構想，比如舞曲、像《天球、彗星は夜を跨いで》那樣的搖滾等。我考慮了很久，第一首作詞作曲的歌曲應該是什麼樣的，但要實際輸出自己的想法比想像中困難很多。所以最後我先從腦中浮現的旋律開始擴展，創作過程中同時出現了歌詞，然後慢慢完成了這首歌。主題則變成了這樣一個信息：「對於那些選擇放棄的人，我想說，如果在那時候放棄了，那比賽就真的結束了。」

——就是「因為討厭你說的那種漂亮話（綺麗事），所以我才唱歌」這段歌詞吧？感覺星街桑平時也常有這樣的感受？

星街：真的非常有這種感覺。我從小就在上網，會加入各種各樣的社群。但大多數人都住在都市，所以常會說：「有機會的話一起出去玩吧」、「我們去哪裡哪裡吧」之類的話。可是我住得離市區很遠，沒辦法輕易地過去。後來我搬到都市裡，心想：「終於可以自由行動了！」就聯絡了以前關係很好的朋友，結果對方卻說：「我年紀大了，會很累。」確實，對方的年紀在我還是孩子那時就已經是個大人了，所以我也能理解，但還是覺得有點難過。

——把放棄或隱藏真心話當成漂亮話的一種吧。

星街：每次聽到這種放棄的言論，我都會告訴自己絕對不要變成那樣。不論年紀多大，我都想保持年輕的心，想穿喜歡的衣服、想玩遊樂園的雲霄飛車。我永遠都想保有童心。所以我在配信時也會常說「不要放棄」之類的話，但其實我也覺得這句話本身也是一種漂亮話。我討厭別人對我說漂亮話，也討厭自己說漂亮話，所以我就乾脆唱歌。

——這首歌的作曲過程是怎麼樣的？

星街：一開始我打算自己用電腦軟體編曲。先決定好和弦，然後邊聽伴奏邊哼出旋律。但後來發現太困難了，而且截稿日期又快到了，只好先把副歌的部分哼出來，然後跟井上拓先生說：「抱歉，我只做到這裡了。」他就幫我配上了編曲，然後我再繼續填詞和作曲。

——原來如此，感覺你們之間來回溝通了很多次呢。

星街：井上先生跟我說：「剛收到你哼的那一小段時，我還想說要怎麼處理呢。」（笑）不過最後還是順利完成了。

——之後還會想繼續作詞作曲嗎？

星街：當然！我腦中已經有好多點子了，要更努力才行。我覺得這次的作品只完成30%。最近我一直在把喜歡的歌曲加入書籤，想要多聽多學。

——多聽多看確實是很重要的。隨著專輯發行，您的曝光度也會增加吧？聽說您的Spotify廣告在紐約時代廣場播放了。

星街：對啊，這件事超有趣的。經紀人跟我說的時候，我還以為是在澀谷那個呢。

——（澀谷的）スクランブルスクエア(Scramble Square)（笑）。

星街：我當時還想說：「時代廣場是哪裡啊？」（笑）

——雖然網路沒有實體距離的限制，但VTuber的社會滲透以及向現實世界的拓展，我覺得對妳所提倡的活動主題來說意義重大。

星街：真的非常有意義。我聽說日本只有少數幾位創作者可以在時代廣場打廣告，而且我還是個獨立創作者，這真的太不可思議了。我覺得這代表著一個新時代的來臨。

—— 2月1日，您將迎來在日本武道館的個人演唱會【Hoshimachi Suisei 日本武道館 Live “SuperNova”】。這正是您從個人活動時期的第一支自我介紹影片中就夢想的目標。

星街： 感慨萬分。尤其這是我用了7年時間追逐的夢想，所以也曾擔心實現夢想後會不會燃燒殆盡。

—— 的確如此。

星街： 我也曾擔心，實現這個夢想後，聽眾們會不會像看完一部故事後就離開了。但其實，現在的我已經規劃好了武道館之後的未來，也確信聽眾們會一直陪伴著我。這次武道館之所以能成為現實，是因為我決定不讓這個夢想留在「未完成」的狀態，而是勇敢地邁出腳步。

—— 這是一個通過點呢。

星街： 是的，我想這次成功地將它變成了一個通過點。

—— 最後，能分享一下關於未來的展望嗎？

星街： 從以前到現在，我的目標一直是讓「虛擬存在」成為理所當然的世界。我喜歡《電腦線圈》那種未來科幻的感覺，也希望能在有生之年看到那樣的未來。而我能做到的，就是努力開拓自己的道路，讓更多人認識到這份價值。

——如果用百分比來衡量目前的進程，您覺得現在大概完成了多少呢？

星街：我記得之前在其他地方也被問過類似的問題，好像回答的是39%。目前還只是39%。針對虛擬的存在，有些人會說「這樣很奇怪吧」或者「根本沒必要出現在台前吧」，但每次看到這些話，我都會覺得「這些人對虛擬的認知還不夠啊」。

——可以說是從了解這一步開始就拒絕了。

星街：可能是因為誇大了不好的部分、缺點的部分吧。例如有人說「按個按鈕就可以跳舞或唱歌吧」，但事實根本不是這樣啊。既然如此，我覺得即使會讓人覺得討厭，我也會通過擴大自己的活動範圍，強行把這些東西塞進大家的視線裡，讓他們「看吧看吧，這就是虛擬」。這樣一來，對虛擬的認知自然也會隨之提升吧。所以，我會努力讓自己活躍起來，創造更多的機會，讓更多人有機會接觸到我們。

（全文完。）

Billboard JAPAN

January 2025

Hoshimachi Suisei Interview

“I was worried I might burn out.”

—The album presents a resilient and powerful human image fitting for its revolutionary concept, but tracks like “Caramel Pain” and “DEADPOOL feat. KAF” stand out with a sense of shadow and uniqueness. What are your thoughts on this?

Hoshimachi: I approached each song individually, and in the end, I felt like the whole album came together nicely. For “Caramel Pain”, the discussion during the meetings was actually quite brief. When I asked, “Do you need more input from me?” they responded, “You might create something better if you have more freedom.” So, I was given a lot of creative liberty. The result was a song that really felt like me, and I thought it turned out great.

—What about “DEADPOOL feat. KAF”?

Hoshimachi: I had previously collaborated with KAF on a cute, pop song called “Issei Fūbi”. So this time, I wanted to create something entirely different—something that wasn’t overly catchy or trendy. I aimed for the opposite direction. Both songs were challenging in their own way, though.

—It seems like you didn’t assemble the album with the overall balance in mind from the beginning.

Hoshimachi: That’s right. It was really about focusing on each individual track. My first and second albums were created in the same way—I would just make songs I wanted to, and then later worry about how the album would come together as a whole. I would often think, “Can I really make this work?” but in the end, it always managed to come together. This time was no different. I think the consistency throughout the album is thanks to the creators who worked with me and their understanding of who I am.

—This album also includes “Kireigoto”, a song you wrote and composed yourself. Was this your first attempt at creating your own song?

Hoshimachi: Yes, it was my first time.

—What inspired you to take this step?

Hoshimachi: I wanted to try during my second album, but I couldn’t manage it in time. Or rather, I couldn’t get myself to start. When discussing the third album, I said, “I really want to do it this time,” and before I knew it, deadlines were being set.

—You had no way out.

Hoshimachi: Exactly. I had no choice but to make it. Even so, I ended up missing the deadline significantly multiple times (laughs). But I managed to finish it in the end.

—Did you have a theme in mind at first?

Hoshimachi: I had a lot of ideas for the kind of songs I wanted to create, like dance music or something like the rock style of “Tenkyū, Suisei wa Yoru o Mataide”. But when it came to my first attempt at songwriting, I thought hard about what kind of song would be most appropriate. It turned out to be much harder than I expected to put my ideas into words and music. So, I decided to abandon themes for the time being and instead build upon melodies that came to mind. The first phrase of the chorus came to me with lyrics, and I expanded it from there. The theme ended up being a message to people who are ready to give up—essentially, the idea that “If you give up now, it’s game over.”

—The part where you sing, “I hate the mouth that spews pretty words (Kireigoto) so I’ll sing instead,” really resonates. Does this reflect your personal thoughts?

Hoshimachi: Absolutely. I’ve been active on the internet for a long time and have encountered many communities. Most people lived in cities, so they could easily say, “Let’s hang out” or “Let’s meet up somewhere,” but I lived far away from urban areas and couldn’t join them easily. When I eventually moved to the city and thought, “Now I can finally be free,” I reached out to an old friend, only to be told things like, “I’m too old for that now.” I understand that friend was already an adult back when I was a kid, still, it was really sad to hear that.

—So, the song reflects the resignation and superficiality of those kinds of words?

Hoshimachi: Yes, every time I heard those kinds of words, I told myself, “I don’t want to end up like that.” No matter how old I get, I want to stay fresh, wear cool clothes, enjoy amusement parks, and ride roller coasters. I want to hold on to my youthful spirit. I often tell my listeners during my streams not to give up, but even I recognize that my words can be seen as pretty and superficial. That’s why I thought, “Fine, I’ll just sing about it.”

—How did the composition process go?

Hoshimachi: At first, I thought I’d do it digitally on a computer program—determine the chords, play the accompaniment, and then add a melody. But it turned out to be too difficult. As the deadline approached, I created the chorus through humming and handed it over, saying, “I’m sorry, but this is all I’ve got.” TAKU INOUE built the track from there, and I continued adding melodies and lyrics afterward.

—It sounds like there was a lot of back-and-forth.

Hoshimachi: Mr. INOUE told me, “When you first sent just one phrase, I wasn’t sure how to proceed,” but we made it work in the end.

—Do you plan to continue writing and composing your own songs?

Hoshimachi: Definitely. I have so many ideas and want to improve. This time, I feel like I achieved about 30% of my potential. Lately, I’ve been bookmarking songs I find inspiring as part of my research.

—It’s important to keep learning. Speaking of milestones, we heard your image is being featured in a Spotify billboard in Times Square, New York (starting January 24).

Hoshimachi: This is funny—when my manager told me, I initially thought it was in Shibuya.

—The (Shibuya) Scramble Square! (laughs)

Hoshimachi: I got mixed up! I even asked, “What’s Times Square again?”

—The physical distance of the internet doesn’t always matter, but this is a big milestone for VTubers and their presence in the real world.

Hoshimachi: It’s huge. I heard only a few Japanese artists have had this opportunity. It feels like we’re ushering in a new era.

—On February 1, you’ll also be performing at the Nippon Budokan for Hoshimachi Suisei Nippon Budokan Live “SuperNova”. Achieving your dream of performing at the Budokan must feel surreal.

Hoshimachi: It’s incredibly emotional, but because this has been my dream for seven years, I did worry about burning out afterward.

—Understandable.

Hoshimachi: I also worried that my audience might feel like they’ve reached the end of the story and start leaving. About two years ago, I was asked, “If the Budokan becomes available, would you want to perform there?” I wanted to, but I also wondered if it was better to leave it as an unfulfilled dream. However, in the end, I decided to leave my mark and move forward.

—It’s a milestone.

Hoshimachi: Exactly, and now I have a clear vision for what comes after Budokan. I’m very busy, but it’s reassuring to know my fans will stick with me. I’m excited to step onto that stage.

——Finally, could you share your vision for the future?

Hoshimachi: I’ve always said this, but my goal is to make virtual existences a normal part of the world. I love futuristic sci-fi like Dennou Coil, and I’d love to help create a world like that during my lifetime. For now, I’ll keep pushing forward and doing my part.

——If you were to measure your journey in terms of percentage, how far do you think you’ve come at this point?

Hoshimachi: I’ve been asked a similar question elsewhere, and I think I answered 39%. I’d say it’s still just 39%. There are still many people who throw comments like “Isn’t this kind of weird?” or “There’s no need for something like this to be in the spotlight,” at virtual existence. Every time I see such comments, I often feel, “Their understanding of this is not very clear.”

――It’s like they’re rejecting it from the very step of getting to know it.

Hoshimachi: Perhaps they exaggerate the bad parts or flaws. For example, when people say things like, “You just press a button to dance or sing, right?” I think, “That’s not how it works at all.” In that case, I don’t mind if they find it annoying—I’ll keep expanding my activities, forcing it into their awareness, and saying, “Here, take it. This is what virtual is.” If I keep doing that, I believe people will naturally gain a clearer understanding. That’s why I’ll keep working hard, staying active, and creating opportunities for as many people as possible to come into contact with this.

(This concludes the interview.)

title: Billboard JAPAN 2025年1月 星街彗星訪談 Part 2 嘗試邁出網路圈的一步 ——在先前的訪談中，提到過《GHOST》的進化版本是《Specter》，那麼在《新…
context:
Billboard JAPAN

2025年1月

星街彗星訪談

Part 2

嘗試邁出網路圈的一步

——在先前的訪談中，提到過《GHOST》的進化版本是《Specter》，那麼在《新星目錄》中是否也有什麼起點或核心歌曲呢？

星街：嗯……應該是《AWAKE》吧。

——那是一首誕生得比較早的歌曲嗎？

星街：不，也不是這樣。如果這麼說的話，應該是《先驅者》是最早的一首。不過，專輯的概念大致確立下來的，應該是從《Bibbidiba》這首歌開始的。我們決定明確以「革命」為主題來製作專輯，而《AWAKE》正是這種感覺的濃縮體現。

——歌詞中有像「start to know 革命的狼煙は／start to go 変化を恐れない覚悟さ」這樣的句子。這首歌的作曲與編曲是由 Giga 和 TeddyLoid 共同完成的。

星街：我想創作一首關於「堅強女性」的歌曲。像《Bibbidiba》也是如此。因為我個人本來就性格比較強，所以當想融入我的個人風格時，歌詞和曲調自然就會變成這種形象。這兩位作曲家非常擅長創作具有核心意志的歌曲，可以很好地表現堅強女性的特質。我覺得這對搭檔真的是最棒的組合。

——在製作過程中，你們是怎麼交流的？

星街：我傳達的想法是「強調堅強女性，具有攻擊性的歌曲」。現在的女性很向往、也很崇拜堅強的女性。比如歌詞裡的「定型文のstoryteller micは渡しちゃ駄目」（千篇一律的說故事人，話筒可不能交給他們），這句我特別喜歡。我自己也不喜歡被固定的框架束縛，所以希望探索出屬於自己的方式。不能將舵交給那些只會按模板行事的人。

——聽到這裡，「先驅者」「Bibbidiba」「AWAKE」作為專輯開頭的這種銜接就非常具有象徵意義了。

星街：是的。一開始我們確實討論過將《Bibbidiba》放在專輯的第一首，因為這首歌已經大紅了。不過考慮到整體概念後，還是覺得《先驅者》或《AWAKE》更符合「革命」這個主題，這樣更能傳達我們的想法。

——參與這張專輯製作的創作者陣容也非常多元且豪華。像是《先驅者》的山內總一郎，以及《ビーナスバグ，Venus Bug》的川谷繪音等，他們的參與是否引起了很大的反響？

星街：在第2張專輯之前，主要是邀請在網路圈活躍的創作者們合作。因為我自己從很早以前就接觸網路，當時請來的也多是我在那裡聽過的創作者。不過這次的第3張專輯，在保持概念不變的前提下，我們討論過要嘗試邁出網路圈的一步。川谷繪音正是這樣的例子之一。我一直很喜歡「極品下流少女」這支樂團，他們的音樂當初給我的感覺非常新穎。所以我很好奇，像繪音桑這樣的創作者，在當今這個時代會為我寫出什麼樣的歌曲，因此向他發出了邀請。

——在你看來，川谷先生的音樂有什麼樣的特徵呢？

星街：雖然我對音樂類型沒有很深入的了解，但我覺得他創作的歌曲都非常時尚。而且他參與了很多不同的樂團，每支樂團的音樂風格都不同，但又能夠保留屬於他自己的特點，我覺得這非常厲害。

——這次合作中，你向他提出了哪些要求呢？

星街：我們的會議應該是在 2023 年 12 月左右，我記得那時的結論是讓繪音桑以自己的方式去解釋星街彗星這個形象。

——這算是比較交由他自由發揮的方式嗎？

星街：可能是吧。不過在我介紹自己時，經常會用到「星」或者「夜空」這類關鍵詞。但因為以星星為主題的歌曲已經越來越多了，所以當時也有考慮把焦點放在「街」這一部分上。《Venus Bug》或許就是這種風格的歌曲。比如像歌詞中的「渋谷5時」。

——《Bibbidiba》和《AWAKE》的MV將實拍與動畫結合，取景地也是都市的街景呢。

星街：我確實有一種想融入現實、走向更廣闊的世界的心情。作為虛擬的存在，我常常思考如何更好地接觸現實中的人們，最後得出的結論是「融合」。我的這種想法得到了所有創作者們的理解與支持。

——《Venus Bug》的MV也已經公開了。

星街：是我自己提議要用全實拍的方式來拍攝的。這首歌的概念非常有趣，影片中很多人都在哼唱《Venus Bug》。而歌詞中的「私、今誰かになれそうな気がしたの」（我現在感覺自己能成為某個人）正是這首歌的靈感來源。

——這次錄製專輯中，你覺得最具挑戰性的歌曲是哪首？

星街：《繭と心》這首歌因為是變拍子的，所以錄製過程相當不容易。此外，高音部分也很有挑戰性，我努力以自然的方式完成了這些部分。

——《Caramel Pain》是由 PEOPLE 1 的 Deu 提供的歌曲，這首歌中你在不同段落中切換了完全不同的歌唱方式，非常耐人尋味。

星街：這首歌的錄製過程中，Deu 先生親自來指導。他現場示範了某些部分，我們就以此為參考來錄音。他還說了一句很有趣的話：「請像渡我被身子一樣唱。」那是一種反派的感覺（笑）。

(Part 3 待續。)

Billboard JAPAN

January 2025

Hoshimachi Suisei Interview

Part 2

Stepping Out of the Net

――In a previous interview, you mentioned that “Specter” is the evolved form of “GHOST.” Was there a starting point or core track for Shinsei Mokuroku as well?

Hoshimachi: Hmm… I’d say “AWAKE.”

――Was it one of the earlier tracks to be created?

Hoshimachi: Not really. In that sense, “Pioneer” came first. However, the album’s concept began to take shape around “Bibbidiba” That’s when we decided to consciously create with a theme of “revolution.” That spirit is especially captured in “AWAKE.”

――The phrase “start to know the signal of revolution / start to go the resolve to face change without fear” is quite striking. The track was composed and arranged by Giga and TeddyLoid.

Hoshimachi: I wanted to create a song about a “strong woman.” “Bibbidiba” had a similar vibe. I consider myself to be quite strong-willed, so when I infused my personality into it, it naturally ended up with such lyrics and tone. These two are brilliant at writing songs with a strong core and a sense of purpose, and this duo is truly the best.

――What kind of communication took place during production?

Hoshimachi: I told them I wanted a song that emphasizes a strong woman and has an aggressive vibe. Nowadays, people admire and are drawn to strong women. The line “don’t hand the mic to the formulaic storyteller” is one of my favorites. I dislike conforming to molds. I want to find my own way. You shouldn’t entrust your course to people who follow templates.

――Hearing all of this, the flow of the album’s opening with “Pioneer,” “Bibbidiba,” and “AWAKE” feels very symbolic.

Hoshimachi: Exactly. Initially, there was talk of putting “Bibbidiba” first since it had gone viral, but considering the overall concept, I felt that starting with either “Pioneer” or “AWAKE” would better convey the revolutionary message.

――The creators involved in this album are diverse and stellar. “Pioneer” features Souichiro Yamauchi, while “Venus Bug” was composed by Enon Kawatani. These collaborations must have garnered a lot of attention.

Hoshimachi: My first two albums primarily featured creators active in the internet circle, as I’ve been immersed in that world for a long time and asked people whose music I had been listening to. For this third album, while keeping the concept intact, I wanted to step out of the net world. One of the names that came up during this discussion was Enon Kawatani. I’ve always loved Gesu no Kiwami Otome, and their music was revolutionary when it first appeared. So, I was curious about what kind of song Enon-san would write for me in today’s era, and that’s why I approached him.

――What is your impression of Kawatani-san’s music?

Hoshimachi: I’m not well-versed in music genres, but I think of him as someone who creates stylish music. He’s involved in various bands, each with its unique vibe, showcasing his versatility. Yet, no matter the style, there’s always a distinctive Kawatani touch, which I find incredible.

――What kind of requests did you make for this collaboration?

Hoshimachi: I believe we had the meeting around December 2023. I think we agreed on letting Kawatani-san interpret Hoshimachi Suisei in his own way.

――Was it more or less left to him?

Hoshimachi: Perhaps. When I talk about myself, I often use keywords like stars or the night sky. However, there came a time when I wanted to shift the focus to the “city” side of Hoshimachi. “Venus Bug” leans in that direction—it even references “Shibuya at 5.”

――The music videos for “Bibbidiba” and “AWAKE” combine live-action and animation, with urban cityscapes as their backdrop.

Hoshimachi: I have a strong desire to integrate into the real world and make an impact. As a virtual presence, I’ve been thinking a lot about how to better approach people in the third dimension. The answer I arrived at was “fusion.” The creators involved understood and brought that vision to life.

――The music video for “Venus Bug” is also out now.

Hoshimachi: I requested to film it entirely in live action. The concept is fascinating—it depicts various people singing “Venus Bug.” The lyrics include a line “I feel like I can become someone else right now,” and the concept was developed from there.

――Were there any tracks that challenged you vocally during recording?

Hoshimachi: “Mayu to Kokoro” was tough because of its irregular meter. Plus, the high notes were demanding, so I worked hard to hit them naturally.

――“Caramel Pain” was provided by Deu of PEOPLE 1. Each section of the song showcases a different vocal approach, making it very engaging.

Hoshimachi: Deu-san directed the recording session in person. He would sing examples and say, “Do it like this,” which I used as references. At one point, he asked me to “sing like Toga Himiko.” It was a fun challenge—like embodying a villain.

(Continues on Part 3.)

This year, I’m trying to give myself more free time. I’ve turned down a lot of work. 今天供給太多真的讓我夠吃一個月了。先是咪口看了彗醬工商後自己也要開，還要特別強調不是工商（說好的只爲商業呢？），然後彗醬看到咪口開瑪車練習後自己也要緊急開台，緊急到封面都來不及作。一堆傳信鴿但彗醬完全不討厭還很高興，因為她自己就狂撿咪口相關留言來回答，變成撿越多鴿子越多，又補了更多mcmt整人的細節⋯整晚聊好多咪口。還直接大方在配信中同時視聽咪口配信。自己都變指示廚了。雖然她嘴巴講我幹嘛要配咪口耐久，但感覺就在拖時間陪咪口。說到底妳從一開始突然在咪口開台的時候也緊急開台意圖就很明顯了。而且看得出彗醬其實很想合練，可能是考慮到咪口那是視聽者參加型的所以不去打擾吧⋯總之我已經要被糖淹沒了⋯

Today’s sugar supply is sufficient that I can live on it for at least a month. First we had Miko did a stream totally because of Suichan’s sponsored stream, yet Miko had to make it clear that her stream wasn’t sponsored like Suichan’s (what about when you said you guys would do something like this only if it was business related ?) Then Suichan decided to do an emergency Mario Kart stream because she saw Miko was doing one, it’s so urgent that she didn’t have time to do a stream thumbnail. There were many messenger pigeons in the chat but Suichan wasn’t mad at all, because she actually cherry picked questions related to Mikochi to reply to, so the more she picked the more pigeons came in. Suichan also gave more details regarding the mcmt pranks…she talked about Miko a lot the entire night. Suichan wasn’t shy about letting the chat knew she’s actually watching Miko’s stream simultaneously. Suichan herself actually became a backseat driver to Miko’s practice session. Even though Suichan said why would she stay here all night to accompany Miko, you can sense Suichan actually wanted to stay. It’s quite obvious since she opened the emergency stream from the beginning, and you can tell Suichan was looking for chances to join Miko. But maybe because Miko’s stream allowed viewers participation so Suichan didn’t want to interfere…anyways I am still buried by loads of sugar…
2019年7月26日。那時的彗醬正在進行INNK活動。雖然只是來自咪口的一句簡單的加油，但這是歷史上咪口第一次回覆彗醬的推特。可以看到彗醬非常激動，連用了六個尖叫。在此之前，彗醬已經在推特五次標記或提到咪口但皆無獲得回應。順帶一提，第五次就是彗醬說出那句名言「咪口醬今天也很可愛」的那次。

July 26th, 2019. Suichan was busy with INNK activities. Even though it was a brief message to cheer for Suichan, it was the first tweet ever from Mikochi. As you can see Suichan was overwhelmed. She screamed six times. Suichan has either tagged or mentioned Mikochi five times on twitter prior to this but have yet received a reply. Another fun fact here: the fifth time Suichan mentioned Mikochi, that was when she wrote the famous quote ”Mikochan is cute today too”.
